entities.name: SoftBank Group
entities.zh: ソフトバンクグループ
entities.desc: Masayoshi Son's investment holding company and Tokyo's primary listed proxy for the global AI-infrastructure trade (via Arm, the OpenAI/Stargate commitments and Vision Fund AI bets) — distinct from the listed telecom SoftBank Corp (TSE: 9434). Fell 11.46% to ¥5,278 on July 24, 2026 as Alphabet's raised capex guidance repriced the AI-infrastructure trade. Separately, SoftBank has been enlisted as part of Japan's outbound AI diplomacy, attending the first Japan–France high-level AI talks in Paris in June 2026 alongside Sakana AI. **$40B OpenAI bridge loan widens (#59, Jul 27, 2026):** The 12-month bridge loan backing SoftBank Vision Fund 2's $30B follow-on OpenAI investment attracted 21 additional lenders in wider syndication, absorbing roughly $7B of the facility — First Abu Dhabi Bank, GIC and Standard Chartered each took close to $1B, with the remainder split among European, Japanese and Taiwanese banks. Signed in March 2026 and in general syndication since May, the loan carries a margin of ~250bp over SOFR (~6.14% all-in) and leaves underwriters/senior lenders holding the remaining $33B; the arranger group is expected to earn $100M+ in fees. The loan funds the second $10B OpenAI tranche executed July 1 and a further $10B planned for October.

tags.l: Core member of Noetra physical-AI consortium
Trades on US hyperscaler capex sentiment

entities.name: NEC Corporation
entities.desc: Japan's largest system integrator. Anthropic's first Japan-based Global Partner; deploying Claude Opus across ~30,000 NEC Group engineers via BluStellar Scenario platform. Member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (10%+ equity). Runs dual-stack hedge: backs sovereign domestic model while distributing Claude for enterprise and government — SOC services for finance, manufacturing, and local government sectors. **Noetra consortium (#17, #29, #31):** Founding member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (Noetra) with >10% equity stake alongside SoftBank, Sony, Honda. Pattern setter for Japanese IT integrators to add domestic model exposure alongside US frontier models.

entities.name: Fujitsu
entities.desc: Japan's largest IT services firm. **Dual frontier AI partnership (May 27, 2026):** Signed resale + integration agreements with both OpenAI (ChatGPT Enterprise, Codex) and Anthropic (Claude) — largest Japanese IT integrator now official dual-frontier AI distributor covering government ministries and enterprise. Sets the pattern for NEC, Hitachi, NTT to follow. **AI Foundation Model Consortium (Issue #17):** Confirmed equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. — brings government and enterprise customer distribution to the domestic model project. Also member of MHI + PFN + Fujitsu supply chain for defense/critical infrastructure AI. **Dual AI partnership (#4, May 2026):** Reseller for both OpenAI (ChatGPT Enterprise, Codex) and Anthropic (Claude) across government ministries and enterprise clients. **Noetra consortium (#17, #29, #31):** Equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Dev Co. (Noetra); brings government distribution + enterprise client base. **FSA compliance beneficiary (#24, #26):** Positioned for Q3 contract acceleration as non-compliant foreign-API routers face regulatory exposure. **Kozuchi Multi AI Agent Framework (#44, Jul 2026):** Self-evolving multi-agent platform for enterprise AI — automates configuration of agent teams from business knowledge documents, then continuously restructures based on execution results and human feedback. Early customer verification trials launched Jul 15, 2026. Addresses Japan's AI talent shortage (人材不足) by eliminating need for ML engineers to build agent plumbing. Competes in integration tier alongside NTT Data and NEC, one layer above Noetra's foundation model. **Watt-Bit distributed AI infrastructure PoC (#58, Jul 27 2026):** Fujitsu joined Nautilus Technologies, Internet Initiative Japan (IIJ), TEPCO Power Grid and Chubu Electric Power Grid in a NEDO-backed demonstration of a next-generation distributed AI processing infrastructure built around an all-photonics network (APN) — power-utility fiber plus Fujitsu/1FINITY communications equipment linking GPU servers across two utilities' supply areas. Test case: real-time 4K video and telemetry from the KYOJO CUP formula-car finale at Fuji Speedway, routed over low-latency, high-bandwidth links. Framed as proof-of-concept for Japan's 'watt-bit' (ワット・ビット) vision — treating distributed AI compute as a flexible load resource for grid supply-demand balancing, a genuinely different angle from Fujitsu's prior robotics/agentic-AI announcements.

tags.l: Watt-Bit AI infra PoC w/ TEPCO, Chubu (Jul 27)

entities.name: Sony AI
entities.desc: Sony Group AI subsidiary. Member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (10%+ equity). Research focus covers robotics, gaming AI, and imaging intelligence. Sony's hardware ecosystem (PlayStation, cameras, sensors) provides unique data sources for physical AI training.

entities.name: Preferred Networks (PFN)
entities.zh: プリファードネットワークス
entities.desc: Japan's leading deep learning AI startup. PLaMo foundation models, MN-Core AI processors, PFCP cloud platform. Engineers seconded to SoftBank physical AI JV (announced April 2026). **MHI + PFN Business Alliance (Issue #7, Jun 2, 2026):** Alliance signed with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries for joint development of AI for mission-critical machinery — social infrastructure + national security/defense. PFN contributes PLaMo models and MN-Core AI processors; MHI contributes aerospace, defense, and energy hardware. Policy framing: Japan-made AI for keizai anzenhoshō (経済安全保障, economic security) domains. Capital alliance with MHI targeted within FY2026 (by March 2027). **PLaMo 3.0 Prime (#25, Jun 22 2026):** ¥60 input / ¥250 output per million tokens — less than half comparable US model pricing; trained from scratch on Japanese-heavy data (no foreign base model fine-tune). AI sovereignty (AI主権) framing: FSA audit-trail compliance built-in; targeted at Japan's 3.8M SMBs, financial services, healthcare. **Noetra (#31):** Engineers seconded to SoftBank-led sovereign AI consortium alongside separate MHI defense AI track (#7). **India-Japan AI pact + Sarvam deal (#34, Jul 2026):** India-Japan Summit (Jul 2) produced Joint Statement on AI cooperation. PFN signed commercial agreement with Sarvam (India's government-backed sovereign LLM startup); PFN brings MN-Core accelerators + physical/industrial AI expertise; Sarvam brings India's sovereign-model mandate and fast-growing compute demand. Offers PFN an export channel independent of the domestic Noetra program. No capital commitments or compute numbers disclosed yet; convertibility to MN-Core deployments within 2–3 quarters is the validation checkpoint.

entities.name: NTT Research
entities.desc: Research arm of NTT Group (日本電信電話). Quantum and AI research; Rapidus investor in ¥267.6B funding round. NTT is Japan's national telecom incumbent — provides critical infrastructure for data center connectivity underpinning Japan's AI ambitions.

entities.name: Noetra (Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co.)
entities.zh: 日本AIファウンデーションモデル開発 / Noetra
entities.desc: SoftBank-led sovereign physical AI consortium backed by METI ¥387.3B (five-year; largest single domestic AI commitment in Japan's history). Engineers seconded from SoftBank and Preferred Networks (PFN); AIST providing research coordination. 40+ manufacturing companies committed, including Yaskawa Electric, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Mitsubishi Electric, Tokyo Electron, Asahi Kasei, Daiwa House, SG Holdings. **Goal:** Multimodal physical AI (フィジカルAI) foundation model for robot and industrial machinery control; first model targeted FY2026 (by March 2027); annual updates from manufacturer production-floor data. **Noetra capital close (#29, Jun 29-30 2026):** Second investor tranche (~10 firms) including MUFG, Mizuho, SMBC, Nippon Steel, Kobe Steel, Asahi Kasei, Yaskawa, Fujitsu — total ~34 member organizations. **Competition framing:** Not benchmarking against GPT-4o; competing on physical AI workloads, sovereign data residency, Japanese-language precision, FSA/METI compliance-native architecture. Structural edge: only model trained on Fanuc, Toyota, Kawasaki industrial telemetry foreign models cannot access. NEDO government funding: up to ¥1T over five years (FY2026–FY2030).

entities.name: Rapidus
entities.desc: Japan's state-backed advanced-logic foundry, targeting 2nm GAA mass production at its IIM-1 fab in Chitose, Hokkaido from 2027, built on process technology licensed from IBM and EUV tooling from ASML. Completed a ¥267.6bn funding round from the government and private-sector shareholders in February 2026. DIGITIMES reported on July 24, 2026 that Rapidus is broadening the Chitose cluster beyond the 2nm front-end pilot line to add chip failure analysis and advanced packaging (back-end, 後工程) capability — an attempt to close the gap with TSMC's CoWoS-style integrated front-end/back-end model rather than shipping wafers offshore for assembly.

entities.name: TSMC JASM (Kumamoto)
entities.desc: TSMC-majority JV in Kumamoto, Kyushu. Partners: Sony Group, Toyota, Denso. JASM-1: 6–12nm, production ramping 2024. JASM-2: upgraded to 3nm (approved April 2026), $17B total investment, government covers ~50%. Production target: 2028. Positions Kyushu as Japan's high-end semiconductor cluster alongside Rapidus Hokkaido. Serves automotive AI chip demand (Toyota, Honda, Denso supply chain). **M7.1 Kumamoto earthquake (#61, Jul 28-29, 2026):** A magnitude-7.1 quake (max seismic intensity 5 at the JASM site) struck Kyushu on Jul 28; TSMC evacuated personnel under emergency procedure, then confirmed structural inspections found no damage and resumed JASM-1 operations in stages. JASM-2 (3nm) construction was unaffected structurally but some work was paused as an aftershock precaution. TSMC's Kumamoto output is under 3% of global capacity, so the read-through is more about regional supply-chain fragility than TSMC's own P&L — see Tokyo Electron for the equipment-side exposure.

tags.l: M7.1 quake Jul 28: JASM-1 safe, resumed

entities.name: Kioxia
entities.desc: NAND flash memory maker at the center of the July 2026 chip-complex correction — ~55% off its 2026 peak after the July 16 Waco jury verdict ($229M Viasat patent damages) and a 16% limit-down July 17. At the July 21 reopen after 海の日 it led the rebound, closing +17.2% as the most-bought name in the bargain-hunting session. Q1 FY2026 results due July 31 are the next fundamental checkpoint against the AI-capex scare. **Leveraged-ETF volatility risk (#58, Jul 26-27 2026):** At least nine US-listed leveraged single-stock ETFs tracking Kioxia (issuers include Corgi Strategies, GraniteShares, Tuttle Capital) are nearing launch — the first such products for a Japanese-listed name. Precedent from South Korea is the worry: Seoul's FSC raised leveraged-ETF cash-deposit requirements roughly 3x and suspended new listings after daily-rebalancing flows helped drive Samsung Electronics/SK Hynix volatility to annualized levels near 75%, versus ~37% for the Nikkei 225 and ~13% for the S&P 500. Kioxia has already fallen from a June peak of ¥112,700 to ¥52,500 (Jul 27) amid AI-overinvestment concerns; US leveraged-ETF listings would add a daily-rebalancing flow on top of the existing patent-verdict and earnings overhangs heading into the Jul 31 print. **July 28 plunge to ¥44,550 (#59):** Fell a further 18.3% on July 28 to ¥44,550 (market cap ¥24.41T) as part of a broad Asian semiconductor sell-off, immediate trigger the July 27 STAR Market debut of China's CXMT — which raised $8.6B and surged as much as 472% intraday to a $487B market cap, the largest listing on a mainland Chinese exchange — reviving oversupply and long-run competitiveness concerns for Japanese memory/equipment names just as Kioxia heads into its July 31 Q1 print. **Q1 FY2026 results — record quarter, buyback, net cash (#63, Jul 31 2026):** Revenue ¥1,767.1bn (+76.2% QoQ, +415.5% YoY); non-GAAP operating profit ¥1,326.2bn at a 75% margin — exceeding Kioxia's entire FY2025 operating profit in a single quarter — driven by a ~70% rise in average NAND selling prices and AI-linked data-center/enterprise SSD demand (SSD & Storage segment: ¥1,174.7bn, 66% of revenue, +95.7% QoQ). Company reached a net cash position and announced an ¥800bn share buyback. Shares jumped 17.72% on the print, a sharp reversal from the CXMT-triggered ~60% mid-2026 drawdown and the Viasat verdict overhang — turning Q1 into the AI-capex-durability read-through the market had been waiting for since the Jul 28 sell-off.

entities.name: Tokyo Electron (TEL)
entities.desc: Japan's largest semiconductor equipment maker. Critical supplier of etch, deposition, and cleaning equipment to TSMC, Samsung, Rapidus. Under pressure from US export controls on advanced tool categories. Key beneficiary of Japan's semiconductor manufacturing renaissance. **Nikkei 225 record 72,648 (#23, Jun 22 2026):** TEL price ~¥36,000 → ~10% Nikkei index weight (price-weighted); TEL + Advantest contributed 840+ index points on Jun 22 alone. AI infrastructure investment thesis (Microsoft $10B, AWS ¥2.3T) drives foreign inflows (~¥16T since Apr 2025). TEL Q1 FY2027 earnings (late July): primary readthrough for Rapidus, JASM, Micron Hiroshima equipment order velocity. Also member of Noetra manufacturing coalition (#31).

entities.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
entities.desc: World's largest silicon wafer producer; critical input to TSMC Kumamoto and Rapidus Hokkaido. Also Japan's leading PVC producer. Semiconductor wafer division provides ~70% of silicon wafers used by leading-edge foundries globally.

entities.name: Fanuc
entities.desc: Japan's largest industrial robot and CNC machine maker. May 2026: announced Google Gemini integration enabling natural-language factory control — all future Fanuc robots will be compatible with Google software. Consortium member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV. METI physical AI initiative beneficiary. Key robotics data contributor for Japan's sovereign 物理AI model. **AI Robotics Strategy (#32, Jul 1 2026):** Named as primary OEM supply-chain beneficiary in Japan Revised AI Robotics Strategy (10M AI-equipped robots by 2040 across 18 sectors). Robot deployment gated on Noetra foundation model readiness. **VTLA Physical-AI Dataset Consortium (#33, Jul 2 2026):** Co-founded with Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Yaskawa Electric, Osaka University, and tactile startup FingerVision, under METI/NEDO funding (up to ¥2B over one year). Pooling manufacturing-floor video, tactile (触覚), and motion data toward a shared VTLA (Vision-Tactile-Language-Action) physical-AI model — first time the three largest Japanese robot makers have shared proprietary motion data. Data collected Aug 2026–Jul 2027 from automotive, robotics, and food-production sites.

entities.name: Yaskawa Electric
entities.desc: Top-3 industrial robot maker globally. **AI Foundation Consortium (Issue #17):** Confirmed equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. Strategic significance: Yaskawa's production-floor automation data feeds directly into foundation model training pipeline — validates 'physical AI' framing as structural, not marketing. Core factory automation and motion control product lines remain primary revenue. **Noetra equity stake (#17, #29, #31):** Formal commitment to Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (Noetra); equity stake signals downstream deployment of physical AI models in Yaskawa Motoman systems. Motoman brand: ~20% global collaborative robot market share. Yaskawa's production-floor telemetry data feeds Noetra training pipeline — demand-side validation of the physical AI thesis. One of three primary OEM supply-chain beneficiaries named in Japan Revised AI Robotics Strategy (#32). **VTLA Dataset Consortium (#33, Jul 2026):** Co-founded VTLA physical-AI dataset effort with Kawasaki, Fanuc, Osaka University, and FingerVision (METI/NEDO funded, up to ¥2B). **Q1 FY2026 earnings (#41, Jul 10 2026):** Revenue ¥125.6B (-5.1% YoY), net income ¥6.95B (-24%), EPS ¥26.81 vs ¥35.19 prior year; operating margin 5.5% vs 6.9%. Quarter covers March–May so misses June's JMTBA +52.8% machine-tool order surge — timing mismatch explains divergence. Motion-control and robot order detail is the forward signal to watch in subsequent quarterly prints.

entities.name: JAL × GMO Humanoid Trial (Haneda)
entities.zh: JAL × GMO AI＆ロボティクス
entities.desc: Japan Airlines and GMO AI & Robotics launched a two-year Unitree G1 humanoid robot trial at Haneda Airport in 2026 for baggage, cargo, and cabin operations. First cycle-time data from week of June 1. METI June liability guidelines will be the policy gate determining how quickly pilots convert into scaled commercial operations.

entities.name: Honda Motor
entities.desc: Founding member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (10%+ equity). First designated external deployer of the sovereign physical AI model. Long AI/robotics history (ASIMO humanoid). AI Foundation Model Consortium capital round closing June 2026. Woven City (Toyota JV) adjacent AI infrastructure investment. **Noetra consortium (#29, #31):** Founding member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (Noetra) with >10% equity stake alongside SoftBank, NEC, Sony. Contributes automotive/mobility telemetry to physical AI training pipeline.

entities.name: Nippon Steel
entities.desc: Japan's largest steelmaker. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV consortium (June 2026 capital round). Materials science data (steel properties, processing conditions) key training input for physical AI foundation model. Represents heavy industry capital backing Japan's sovereign AI ambitions.

entities.name: Asahi Kasei
entities.desc: Diversified Japanese chemical and materials conglomerate (TSE: 3407). **AI Foundation Consortium (Issue #17):** Confirmed equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. Materials and healthcare data assets are likely AI training contribution. Earlier covered in the context of industrial AI adoption (Issues #4, #5). **Noetra consortium (#17, #31):** Joined Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (Noetra) as an equity member; spans materials science, synthetic fibers, healthcare; production-process data contributes to Noetra training pipeline.

entities.name: MUFG (Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group)
entities.desc: Japan's largest bank. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (June 2026). Government-authorized to deploy dual AI cyber stack: Anthropic Claude Mythos + OpenAI G-5.5 in tandem. Part of FSA working group on AI-related cyber risks (36 entities, 15 critical infrastructure sectors). Each 25bp BOJ rate hike adds ~¥100–150B in annual net interest income across the three megabanks. **Noetra consortium (#29, Jun 29-30 2026):** Small equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (Noetra); part of second investor tranche (tens of millions of yen). FSA AI compliance guidelines (#24, #26) create dual obligation as both compliance subject and potential procurement beneficiary.

entities.name: Mizuho Financial Group
entities.zh: みずほフィナンシャルグループ
entities.desc: Japan's third-largest bank. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (June 2026). Government-authorized for dual Claude Mythos + OpenAI G-5.5 AI cyber stack. BOJ rate normalization is structurally bullish for NII expansion. **Noetra consortium (#29):** Small equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (second investor tranche). FSA AI compliance guidelines take effect July 1, 2026.

entities.name: SMBC (Sumitomo Mitsui Banking)
entities.desc: Japan's second-largest bank. Government-authorized for dual AI cyber stack alongside MUFG and Mizuho. FSA working group participant. BOJ rate hike of 25bp adds ~¥100–150B NII across the three megabanks. **Noetra consortium (#29):** Small equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (second investor tranche). FSA AI compliance guidelines take effect July 1, 2026.

entities.name: Bank of Japan (BOJ)
entities.desc: Japan's central bank. Governor: Kazuo Ueda (植田和男). Policy rate: 0.75% (held April 2026, 6–3 vote split). Raised FY2026 core CPI forecast to 2.8% from 1.9%. OIS pricing June 2026: 77% probability of 25bp hike to 1.00% at June 15–16 MPM. Three dissenters favoured immediate hike. OECD projects 2.0% by end-2027. JGB purchase commitment signal at June MPM is the key 'hawkish rates / dovish duration' watch. **Q2 2026 Tankan (#31, #32, Jul 1 2026):** Large manufacturer DI +22 (vs. +16 consensus; beat by 6 pts; highest since 2018). Non-manufacturer DI +37 (highest since 1991). Capex actual +11.5% FY2026/27. Recurring profits guidance -6.7% (capex-despite-margin-pressure confirms automation bet). BOJ raised policy rate to 1.00% Jun 16; July 30-31 MPM next key date. AI-specific survey items added in 2026 Tankan — first explicit capex monitoring for AI infrastructure. **JGB yield milestones (#33, #35, Jul 2026):** 10-year JGB new-issue coupon set at 2.7% (29-year high) in Jul 2 MoF auction. Yield then hit 2.81% on Jul 3 (30-year high) on fiscal concerns under PM Takaichi. By mid-July trading near 2.9% (30-year-plus high). Nikkei whipsawed 2,100 points intraday Jul 3; higher JGB yields simultaneously tighten financial conditions and validate the rate-normalization thesis supporting financials. **June PPI 7.1% (#42):** Corporate goods prices +7.1% YoY in June — keeps BOJ rate-hike bets pointed at October even as July 30-31 MPM expected to hold at 1.00%. **MUFG milestone (#45, Jul 13 2026):** Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group overtook Toyota as Japan's most valuable listed company by market cap — first bank to top the league table in a generation. Proximate driver: BOJ at 1.00% (three-decade high) + 10-year JGB near 2.9% (30-year high) reprices bank deposit franchises as earning assets. BOJ July 30-31 Outlook Report: sources indicate likely FY2026 growth upgrade with hold at 1.00%. **Meeting opens amid yen/bond stress (#60, Jul 30 2026):** The two-day policy meeting opens today with consensus still pointing to a hold at 1.00% and an FY2026 growth-forecast upgrade (toward ~0.8%, up from April's 0.5%), supported by resilient AI/semiconductor demand. The decision, due July 31 with Ueda's 3:30pm JST press conference, lands against a weaker yen (near ¥163.7) and a 40-year JGB yield close to its May record — meaning the market-relevant question is less the hold itself than whether Ueda's language leans hawkish enough to validate an autumn hike. **Decision day: hold at 1.00%, GDP forecast upgraded (#61, Jul 31, 2026):** The BOJ held its policy rate at 1.00% as universally expected (52/52 Bloomberg-surveyed economists), closing the two-day meeting that opened Jul 30. The quarterly Outlook Report upgraded the FY2026 real GDP forecast to 0.8% (from April's 0.5%), citing resilient AI/semiconductor-linked capex. With the hold itself priced in, the market-moving variable was Ueda's afternoon press conference — specifically whether his language signals an autumn rate hike is coming sooner than consensus assumes, against a yen near a 40-year low and JGB yields near their May record.

entities.name: Ministry of Finance (MoF)
entities.desc: Japan's fiscal authority. Finance Minister: Satsuki Katayama (片山さつき). Authorized record ¥11.73T (~$74B) FX intervention (為替介入) April 28–May 27, 2026 — first since July 2024, surpassing prior monthly record. USD/JPY hit ¥155 then retraced to 159.3. Issued fresh verbal warnings June 2026. 300bp US-Japan rate gap drives structural yen carry trade pressure. **JGB new-issue coupon 2.7% (#33, Jul 2 2026):** MoF's auction of new 10-year JGB set coupon at 2.7% — highest new-issue coupon in 29 years. Auction described as soft (subscription ratio below prior levels), signaling JGB supply/demand tension as Takaichi's fiscal stance raises long-end vigilance. **Ambush FX intervention (#34, Jul 3–4 2026):** USD/JPY hit four-decade low near 162.8; roughly 1% yen surge occurred in holiday-thinned July 3–4 US trading — consistent with MoF's unannounced 'ambush' intervention tactics (not officially confirmed; MOF has declined to comment). Yen near 1986 lows entering Q3 2026. **Goldman 165 call (#38, Jul 8 2026):** Goldman Sachs cut 12-month USD/JPY forecast to 165 — among Wall Street's most bearish. Thesis: structural carry-trade pressure and US-Japan rate differential keep yen weak despite intervention risk. **GPIF head-fake (#41, Jul 11 2026):** Finance Minister Katayama said government will explore measures encouraging Japan's pension funds to substantially increase domestic asset holdings. Response was immediate: yen firmed toward 161, 10-year JGB yield pulled back from 30-year highs, Nikkei rose 1.2%. Described as a positioning squeeze (kuchisaki kainyū — verbal intervention) — GPIF formal allocation changes move through review processes, not press conferences. Concrete follow-up required to validate.

entities.name: METI (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry)
entities.desc: Japan's industrial policy ministry. Core AI infrastructure funder and semiconductor strategist. ¥1.23T AI/semiconductor budget envelope; ¥387.3B specifically for AI development. Backs Rapidus 2nm semiconductor project (~¥2.35T total government commitment). AI Promotion Act (AI推進法): enacted 2026, innovation-first, voluntary guidelines for most applications. **Genesis Mission (Issue #11, Jun 4–5, 2026):** Japan named first international partner in U.S. DOE Genesis Mission — $1B combined ($500M each) over 5 years; 12 U.S. national labs + 12 Japanese research institutions; quantum technology, nuclear fusion, biotechnology, materials AI, advanced manufacturing. MEXT co-sponsoring. **AI Basic Plan revision (Issue #22, Jun 20, 2026):** Draft revision released for public comment — adds enhanced international cooperation provisions and new cybersecurity plank on AI-enabled cyberattacks. Cabinet approval sought at early date; cybersecurity budget line likely to follow. **Noetra / ¥387.3B commitment (#31):** Largest single domestic AI commitment in Japan's history; ¥300B separately allocated to AI foundation models in FY2026 budget; Noetra's ¥387.3B exceeds prior NEDO AI programs by several multiples. **Revised AI Robotics Strategy (#32, Jul 1 2026):** 10 million AI-equipped robots across 18 sectors by 2040; gated on Noetra model readiness. **FSA AI compliance (#24):** Joint finalization of AI workflow guidelines effective July 1, 2026. **VTLA Dataset Consortium (#33, Jul 2 2026):** METI/NEDO solicitation selected Kawasaki+Fanuc+Yaskawa+Osaka University+FingerVision consortium to build VTLA physical-AI dataset — up to ¥2B over Aug 2026–Jul 2027. Goal: 5,000 hours of video, tactile, and motion data from automotive, robotics, and food-production sites; first multi-vendor standardized physical-AI training corpus in Japan. **Micron Hiroshima subsidy (#35, Jul 4 2026):** METI underwrote up to ¥536B of Micron's ¥1.5T Hiroshima HBM fab (groundbreaking Jul 4). Largest single semiconductor subsidy Japan has authorized; targets HBM supply for AI accelerators. **Japan AX / Second AI Basic Plan (#42, Jul 10 2026):** Prime Minister Takaichi's AI Strategy Headquarters adopted second-phase AI Basic Plan. Brands agenda "Japan AX" (日本AX). Two pillars: vertical AI (sector-specific models) + physical AI. 19 priority fields sorted by marketability, public value, and strategic importance. Orders cross-ministerial regulatory rewrite assuming AI is in the loop. AISI expanded to use frontier models for safety evaluation and cyber defense. Test: late-August FY2027 budget requests — dated line items per priority field determine whether plan has teeth. **Tower Semiconductor grant (#45, Jul 14 2026):** ~$1B in Japanese government grants supporting Tower's $3B silicon photonics + silicon-germanium expansion at Arai facility (300mm conversion).

entities.name: NEDO
entities.zh: 新エネルギー・産業技術総合開発機構
entities.py: Shin-enerugī Sangyō Gijutsu Sōgō Kaihatsu Kikō
entities.desc: METI's innovation-funding agency. Backer of the ¥1tn Noetra foundation-model program and, announced July 22–23, 2026, the Hitachi–Intel–AIST silicon spin-qubit project ('Accelerating the Development and Demonstration of Next-Generation Quantum Computers to Solve Social Challenges', through March 2029). Its project selections are the clearest public map of where Japan's industrial-policy money is flowing in AI, semiconductors and quantum.

entities.name: Digital Agency (デジタル庁)
entities.desc: Established 2021. Leads Japan's digital transformation. Government Gennai (ゲンナイ) generative AI platform launched nationwide May 2026 — government-wide AI deployment. **APPI Amendment (Issue #12, Jun 2026):** Personal Information Protection Act amendment passed lower house; removes individual consent requirement for AI training on medical histories and criminal records. Digital Minister Matsumoto Hisashi used 'AI colony' (AIの植民地) framing — data deregulation as national sovereignty issue. Bill in upper house debate; must clear before parliament rises July 2026. No civil-remedy mechanism — key risk. Primary beneficiaries if passes: healthcare AI, insurance underwriting, enterprise NLP. **APPI revision (#12, #30):** Bill cleared Lower House May 2026; Upper House vote before July 17 Diet recess; allows AI training on pseudonymized personal data without individual consent; Digital Agency / PPC joint review board. Primary beneficiary: Noetra physical AI consortium. **Data center siting (#23):** No MLIT/METI response to Chiba lawsuits as of June 2026; any zoning legislation requires prioritization before Diet recess.

tags.l: Data center siting: no response yet

entities.name: FSA (Financial Services Agency)
entities.desc: Japan's financial regulator. Launched public-private working group on AI-related cyber risks: 36 entities across 15 critical infrastructure sectors. Authorized Japan's three megabanks (MUFG, SMBC, Mizuho) to deploy dual AI cyber stack (Claude Mythos + OpenAI G-5.5). AI cyber governance framework in development. **AI workflow compliance guidelines (#24, #26, #30, Jun 22 2026):** Mandatory audit trails (監査証跡), explainability (説明可能性), and continuous model risk assessment for financial services, healthcare, energy, critical infrastructure. Three-month grace period ended July 1, 2026. Enforcement phase began July 1; examination findings expected Q3 2026 disclosures. Operationalizes AI Promotion Act (AI推進法, passed May 2025) into sector-specific mandates — first enforceable teeth in a major regulated sector.

entities.name: SB OAI Japan GK
entities.zh: SBオープンエーアイジャパン
entities.desc: SoftBank-OpenAI joint venture, established November 2025. **Patching as a Service (launched June 17, 2026):** AI-powered enterprise vulnerability assessment and remediation. Phase 1 target: Japan's top 3,000 companies, focusing on critical infrastructure (airports, power grids, public transit). Technology: OpenAI's specialized cybersecurity models for vulnerability identification; advisory only (not automated code deployment). 50 dedicated security specialists at launch; target 1,000 personnel. Also operates Sarashina API service (launched Nov 2025). Positioned for METI government procurement contracts alongside commercial enterprise revenue. First revenue signal expected in SoftBank August 2026 quarterly earnings. **Patching as a Service (#18, Jun 17 2026):** Commercial launch of AI-powered enterprise vulnerability assessment and remediation planning. Phase 1: Japan's top 3,000 companies, focus on airports, power grids, public transit. 50 dedicated security specialists at launch; target 1,000 personnel. Advisory only (not automated code deployment). Son framed AI cyberattacks as 'Black Ships' (黒船) moment. First revenue signal expected August 2026 quarterly earnings. **OpenAI IPO delay context (#27):** SB OAI Japan GK commercial revenue narrative is SoftBank's partial earnings decoupling argument from Vision Fund marks.

tags.l: Patching as a Service: commercial Jun 2026

entities.name: PKSHA Technology
entities.desc: Tokyo-based AI software company (TSE: 3993). Bridges academic AI research and enterprise deployment in Japan. **Japan AI Index partnership (Issue #10, Jun 4, 2026):** Co-founding partner (with University of Tokyo + Anthropic) of the first Japan AI Index — fixed-point observation framework tracking AI's impact on employment, industries, economy, and education. First report October–November 2026; updates every 3–6 months. PKSHA's structural link to Japanese corporate sector makes it the enterprise deployment conduit for the index's findings. Creates the first credible, non-self-reported AI adoption data series for Japan. **Japan AI Index (#10, Jun 4 2026):** Three-way partnership with University of Tokyo and Anthropic; Claude usage telemetry cross-referenced with MIC/Cabinet Office statistics; first report October-November 2026; designed for comparison with Stanford AI Index and OECD digital adoption metrics. PKSHA bridges research and enterprise deployment.

entities.name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI)
entities.desc: Japan's largest defense and heavy industry manufacturer (TSE: 7011). Aerospace, defense, energy, and industrial systems. **PFN Business Alliance (Issue #7, Jun 2, 2026):** Alliance signed with Preferred Networks for joint development of AI for mission-critical machinery — social infrastructure + national security/defense. MHI contributes aerospace/defense/energy hardware + system integration expertise; PFN contributes PLaMo foundation models and MN-Core AI processors. Use cases: autonomous situational assessment, predictive maintenance, rapid crisis response in high-reliability environments. Policy framing: keizai anzenhoshō (経済安全保障, economic security) — defense customers prefer domestic supply chains. Capital alliance targeted within FY2026 (by March 2027). ITO corporate strategy framework guiding integration. **PFN business alliance (#7, Jun 2 2026):** Capital and business alliance with Preferred Networks (capital stake targeted within FY2026). Scope: joint AI development for mission-critical machinery — social infrastructure + national security/defense. PFN contributes PLaMo foundation models, MN-Core AI processors, PFCP cloud; MHI contributes aerospace, defense, energy hardware. Explicitly framed as Japan-made AI for keizai anzenhoshō (economic security, 経済安全保障) — defense customers prefer domestic supply chains. **GCAP / Edgewing (#36, Jul 3 2026):** £4.6B ($6.1B) GCAP contract awarded to Edgewing JV (BAE Systems + Leonardo + JAIEC, the vehicle backed by MHI). Funds concept/assessment phase + joint detailed design for Japan's next-generation fighter (次期戦闘機). Flying prototype target: end-2027; service entry 2035. First Japanese defense program with genuine export-scale potential. IHI handles engine work (Rolls-Royce collaboration); Mitsubishi Electric takes avionics/sensing workshare. **RV-X reusable rocket (#43, Jul 11 2026):** JAXA + MHI conducted first flight of RV-X reusable rocket testbed at Noshiro Rocket Testing Center. Vehicle: 7.3m long, rose 11m, translated 16m horizontally, set down upright. First flight heritage for reusable propulsion inside MHI — the prime H3 contractor. Follow-on tests planned to ~100m; reusability language entering H3 successor design studies.

tags.l: Economic security (経済安全保障) framing

entities.name: Kawasaki Heavy Industries
entities.desc: Kobe-based heavy industry conglomerate: aerospace, defense, energy, and industrial robots. One of Japan's three primary OEM supply-chain beneficiaries named in the July 1, 2026 Revised AI Robotics Strategy (10M AI-equipped robots by 2040 across 18 sectors, #32). **Noetra coalition (#31):** Participating in METI ¥387.3B physical AI consortium led by SoftBank; production-floor automation data contributes to training pipeline. **Humanoid robot program (#5):** Active development of full-size humanoid robotic systems for manufacturing and hazardous-environment use. **VTLA Dataset Consortium (#33, Jun 27 2026):** Co-founded Vision-Tactile-Language-Action (VTLA) physical-AI dataset standard with Fanuc, Yaskawa, Osaka University, and FingerVision. METI/NEDO backing (up to ¥2B); runs Aug 2026–Jul 2027. Goal: create shared, standardized training data for physical AI from Japanese factory floors — enabling cross-OEM model training without IP leakage. VTLA is Japan's answer to US physical-AI foundation models. **GCAP / Edgewing (#36, Jul 3 2026):** As part of JAIEC (Japan Aerospace Industrial Export Consortium), Kawasaki holds workshare in Edgewing JV alongside BAE Systems + Leonardo. The £4.6B ($6.1B) GCAP contract funds concept/assessment phase + joint detailed design for next-generation fighter; flying prototype by end-2027, service entry 2035. Cross-reference: Issue #32 (AI robotics strategy OEM list); Issue #31 (Noetra coalition member); Issue #5 (humanoid robot program).

entities.name: Mitsubishi Electric
entities.desc: Tokyo. Major electrical equipment and factory automation maker; MELFA industrial robot arm line is a key product. **Noetra coalition (#31):** Member of METI ¥387.3B physical AI consortium; factory automation telemetry from MELFA systems contributes to physical AI training pipeline. Alongside Yaskawa and Kawasaki, forms the core of Japan's industrial robot supply chain feeding into the Noetra model. **GCAP avionics & sensing workshare (#36, Jul 3 2026):** Named as avionics and sensing supplier in the Edgewing JV structure (BAE Systems + Leonardo + JAIEC). The £4.6B GCAP contract allocates systems integration and sensing workshare to Mitsubishi Electric. Flying prototype target: end-2027; service entry 2035. First major defense-export revenue program for Mitsubishi Electric outside the Japanese domestic procurement channel.

entities.name: Sakura Internet
entities.zh: さくらインターネット
entities.desc: Osaka. Japan's leading domestic GPU cloud and data center operator. **AI sovereign cloud (#23, #25):** Named as likely domestic hosting channel for on-premises PLaMo (Preferred Networks) deployments; also partner with Microsoft's $10B Japan AI infrastructure commitment (2026–2029). Structural positioning: sole major GPU cloud operator entirely under Japanese data-residency jurisdiction — critical for FSA compliance-native AI deployments where foreign cloud routing is unacceptable. Cross-reference: Issue #23 (Microsoft/AWS Japan investment context); Issue #25 (PLaMo 3.0 Prime indirect beneficiary). **¥26B Rubin GPU investment, profit forecast raised 6.9x (#64, Jul 28 2026):** Raised its FY2027 (year ending March 2027) net profit forecast to ¥1.5bn — 6.9x the prior year, up from an earlier ¥850m estimate — after Q1 (Apr-Jun 2026) revenue jumped 49% YoY to ¥11.1bn and net profit swung to an ¥855m surplus from a ¥324m loss a year earlier. Unveiled a ¥26bn debt-financed investment in servers equipped with NVIDIA's next-generation Rubin GPUs, delivery scheduled January 2027 — not yet reflected in current guidance, implying further upside once the hardware goes live. Growth drivers: sustained high utilization of GPU cloud services procured in FY2026, plus stable, recession-resistant revenue from its March 2026 selection as a Government Cloud (政府共通クラウド) provider for central/local government systems. Risk: the ¥26bn in new borrowing raises financial leverage, with ROI dependent on generative-AI demand durability and rival cloud operators' capacity additions.

entities.name: NTT Data
entities.desc: Tokyo. Japan's largest IT services company by revenue (subsidiary of NTT Group). **FSA compliance beneficiary (#25, #26, #30):** Named alongside Preferred Networks PLaMo as a primary structural beneficiary of FSA AI workflow compliance guidelines (effective July 1, 2026) — domestically governed models with native Japanese-jurisdiction audit architecture are positioned for Q3 contract acceleration as non-compliant foreign-API routers face regulatory exposure. **Enterprise AI distribution (#25):** Positioned as enterprise deployment partner for PLaMo 3.0 Prime, bringing established government and financial-sector customer base at scale — capabilities PFN is still building. **Frontier-model cyber defense (#44, Jul 12 2026):** Launching AI Cyber Defense Center on Jul 31, 2026, using Anthropic Claude frontier models plus proprietary security-operations datasets. Service targets large Japanese enterprises and government agencies. Positions NTT Data as an operator of Claude for national-security-adjacent use cases — a strategic differentiator from pure PLaMo deployment partners. **NVIDIA Nemotron dependency (#63, reported Jul 20 2026):** NTT Data's own domestic foundation model, tsuzumi 2, is trained in part on NVIDIA Nemotron-Personas-Japan — a synthetic dataset reflecting Japan's demographic and cultural statistics — which the company says measurably improved question-answering accuracy. Also piloting the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit for multi-agent system deployment. Illustrates a structural pattern across Japan's 'sovereign' AI builders: domestic-language models still lean on NVIDIA's open Nemotron stack for training data and tooling, not just chips. Cross-reference: Issue #11 (NTT Research quantum/photonics DOE relationship); Issue #25 (PLaMo 3.0 Prime distribution beneficiary); Issue #26, #30 (FSA compliance catalyst).

tags.l: AI Cyber Defense Center: Jul 31 launch

entities.name: Colt Technology Services
entities.zh: コルト・テクノロジー・サービス
entities.desc: London HQ. Data center developer and network provider. **Inzai data center lawsuit (#23, Jun 21 2026):** Colt's 52-meter data center in Inzai City, Chiba Prefecture (SPV backed by Mitsui & Co., CPP Investments Canada, Fidelity) triggered first data center lawsuit in Japan. Adjacent to a 15-story residential condo; ~25% documented property value decline. Inzai City admitted current rules cannot address the conflict. **Broader implication:** Lawsuit filed alongside Shiroi City (2 suits) and opposition clusters in Saitama, Akishima, Hino, Kodaira, and Tokyo's Koto Ward — establishes legal precedent for Tokyo-metro data center site selection risk. METI/MLIT response pending before Diet recess (Jul 2026). Cross-reference: Issue #23 (Japan AI Basic Plan pledge to be 'most AI-friendly' vs. community rights tension).

tags.l: Inzai: first DC lawsuit in Japan

entities.name: AIST
entities.desc: Japan's national applied-research institute under METI. Operates G-QuAT (Global Research and Development Center for Business by Quantum-AI Technology), a ~¥62bn (~$380M) quantum-AI facility hosting quantum and hybrid quantum-classical computing infrastructure. Named partner in the NEDO-backed Hitachi–Intel silicon spin-qubit project (July 2026), where it will co-build an open cloud platform giving external researchers remote access to experimental silicon quantum hardware and a fabrication ecosystem.

tags.l: Cloud access to silicon quantum hardware

entities.name: FingerVision
entities.desc: Tokyo. Tactile-sensing AI startup founded by Yamaguchi Yamato (山口大和). Develops soft, camera-based tactile sensors that give robots a sense of touch (触覚, shokkaku). **VTLA Dataset Consortium co-founder (#33, Jul 2 2026):** Selected under METI/NEDO solicitation to co-found the Vision-Tactile-Language-Action (VTLA) physical-AI dataset alongside Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Fanuc, Yaskawa Electric, and Osaka University. FingerVision contributes the tactile data component — the 'T' in VTLA — which is the bottleneck missing from most physical-AI training pipelines. Up to ¥2B METI/NEDO funding; Aug 2026–Jul 2027 data collection from automotive, robotics, and food-production sites. Key thesis: tactile sensing is the scarce ingredient in physical-AI training data; FingerVision's sensor tech and IP may become a chokepoint as Japan's sovereign physical-AI program scales.

tags.l: Scarce ingredient: touch data for physical AI

entities.name: SB Neo
entities.desc: Delaware-incorporated US neocloud subsidiary announced by SoftBank on July 2, 2026. Ownership: 51% SoftBank Corp. / 49% SoftBank Group. Target: 10GW of AI datacenter capacity by ~2030 built on Infrinia AI Cloud OS (SoftBank's GPU cloud OS, in beta in Japan since May 2026). **GCAP analog for AI infra (#36, Jul 2 2026):** Formal US vehicle to compete in the AI infrastructure space alongside CoreWeave, Lambda Labs, etc. Key watch: financing structure — how much sits on SoftBank Corp.'s investment-grade balance sheet vs. project-level debt determines market treatment. Needs US hyperscaler anchor customers before FY2027 capacity opens. Delaware incorporation filing and capitalization details due within weeks of announcement. Structural risk: neocloud comparables have repriced sharply on delivery and debt-load concerns.

entities.name: Micron Hiroshima
entities.desc: US memory giant Micron Technology's Hiroshima HBM fabrication facility. **Groundbreaking (#35, Jul 4 2026):** Micron held groundbreaking ceremony for ¥1.5 trillion ($9.4B) Hiroshima HBM fab — targeting high-bandwidth memory (高帯域幅メモリ, HBM) for AI accelerators. METI underwrote up to ¥536 billion in government grants (補助金, hojokin) — the largest single semiconductor subsidy Japan has authorized. Timeline: production ramp targeted early-2030s. Strategic rationale: Japan wants an HBM supply source inside its borders to reduce dependence on Korean producers (SK Hynix, Samsung) for AI chip memory. Announced two days after memory names led a violent Tokyo sell-off (Kioxia -30%+ from June peak), framing the investment as a long-cycle commitment rather than a cycle call. Directly complements METI's Noetra AI infrastructure buildout.

entities.name: Tower Semiconductor Japan
entities.zh: タワーセミコンダクター日本
entities.desc: Japan operations of Israel-based specialty foundry Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ: TSEM). Operates the Arai facility (新井工場, Arai kōjō) in Niigata Prefecture — a legacy analog/mixed-signal fab being converted to 300mm for advanced processes. **$3B silicon photonics investment (#45, Jul 14 2026):** Tower announced $3B expansion plan for Japan, supported by ~$1B in Japanese government grants (補助金). Investment targets silicon photonics (シリコンフォトニクス) and silicon-germanium technology used in AI systems and datacenters — specifically optical interconnects, which become critical when AI clusters scale beyond what copper interconnects can handle. 300mm conversion at Arai facility. METI strategic rationale: silicon photonics is the optical-interconnect layer Japan currently lacks domestically; Tower's niche technology fills a gap in the Noetra/Rapidus supply chain.

entities.name: Seven & i Holdings
entities.zh: セブン＆アイ・ホールディングス
entities.desc: Japan's largest convenience store operator; parent of 7-Eleven Japan (~21,000 stores). **SoftBank AI stake talks (#41, Jul 11 2026):** Bloomberg reported SoftBank and PayPay in talks for up to ¥300B ($1.85B) stake in Seven & i. Sumitomo Mitsui Card may join; new share issuance being considered. Stated rationale: SoftBank wants to apply in-house AI models to store management across the 21,000-store 7-Eleven network and deploy autonomous robots to offset chronic convenience-store (コンビニ, konbini) labor shortages. More measurable logic: payments consolidation — pairing Japan's dominant QR operator (PayPay) with its largest convenience network. Target signing: summer 2026. Context: 7-Eleven Japan is undergoing strategic restructuring following the failed ACT buyout attempt (2024–2025); a SoftBank anchor investment provides capital and a physical-AI deployment surface at national scale. Key watch: whether AI deployment includes concrete KPIs (store counts, robot units, cost-per-store) or remains narrative framing for a payments consolidation deal.

entities.name: Bank of Japan
entities.desc: Central bank; policy rate at 1.0% since the June 16, 2026 hike, the highest since 1995. Heading into the July 30–31 MPM the domestic case is a firming but still sub-target inflation profile (June core-core 1.7%). The external case sharpened on July 23–24, 2026 when the US Treasury's semi-annual currency report explicitly called for further BOJ rate increases, arguing that 'monetary policy normalisation would help anchor inflation expectations and reduce excessive exchange rate volatility.' Sources reporting still points to a hold at 1% in July with an upgraded FY2026 GDP forecast (~0.8% from 0.5%). **Takaichi approval slide raises July 30-31 stakes (#58, Jul 26-27 2026):** A Yomiuri poll (fielded Jul 24-26) put cabinet approval at 57%, down from 69% in June and below 60% for the first time since Takaichi took office; disapproval of the government's cost-of-living response rose to 71% from 56%. The Takaichi cabinet has delayed a decision on cutting the 8% consumption-tax rate on food, a signature pledge, amid intra-party pushback and market unease over fiscal sustainability. Weaker political capital narrows the BOJ's room to hold rates without appearing to defer to a government seen as tolerating inflation — a dynamic worth watching in the July 30-31 statement language and Ueda's press conference. **Fed holds fifth straight meeting (#59, Jul 29, 2026):** The Federal Reserve held its target range at 3.50%–3.75% at its July 28-29 FOMC meeting, as Chair Kevin Warsh cited persistent above-target inflation to justify keeping policy restrictive — removing, for now, any pressure on the BOJ from a diverging Fed easing path. USD/JPY held near ¥163.90 into the announcement. The BOJ's own meeting begins the next day (Jul 30-31), so the two central banks' decisions land within 48 hours of each other, with consensus still pointing to a BOJ hold at 1.00% alongside an upgraded growth forecast in the quarterly Outlook Report.

tags.l: US Treasury publicly urges more hikes
Jul 30–31 MPM: hold expected, forecast upgrade
Takaichi cabinet seen as dovish constraint

entities.name: Ministry of Finance
entities.desc: Japan's finance ministry, owner of FX intervention policy (executed via the BOJ). Under Finance Minister Katayama Satsuki (片山さつき), MOF intervened at record scale in April–May 2026 as the yen breached 160/USD; the moves bought time but did not reverse the trend. With the yen past 163 on July 22, 2026 — the weakest since 1986 — Katayama pledged 'appropriate' and 'decisive' action against excessive moves and said she had confirmed with Washington that intervention remains an option. The open question is whether MOF defends a level that the broader policy mix (1.0% BOJ rate, expansionary fiscal stance) works against.

entities.name: Noetra
entities.desc: Government-backed sovereign physical-AI venture building a Japan-developed multimodal foundation model, with Sony, SoftBank, NEC and Honda as core companies and METI/NEDO support of up to ¥1T over five years (¥387.3B first tranche, FY2026). As of July 17, 2026 the investor group reached 44 companies with Hitachi and Toshiba joining; Hitachi commits proprietary field data (rail, grid, industrial) to training. Roadmap: reasoning model FY2026, omni-modal model FY2028, 'Real-world Native AI' toward FY2030; ~27,500 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs with the data center operating from June 2028.

tags.l: Own compute arrives after frontier labs move
Full R&D launch confirmed July 16 with 44-company roster (#57)

entities.name: Hitachi
entities.desc: Conglomerate spanning IT (Lumada), energy and rail. Selected by NEDO (announced July 22–23, 2026) to lead a silicon spin-qubit quantum computing project with Intel K.K. and AIST, running through March 2029: qubit chips on Intel's 18A process, cryogenic packaging and 3D high-density integration, targeting a 100-qubit prototype by FY2028 and a 1,000-qubit platform by FY2030, with open cloud access via AIST's G-QuAT center. Expands the Hitachi–Intel strategic collaboration announced June 5, 2026. Positions Hitachi on the CMOS-manufacturable quantum modality, distinct from Fujitsu/RIKEN superconducting efforts. **Claude Mythos cybersecurity verification (#60, Jul 28-29 2026):** Hitachi disclosed it has used a preview version of Anthropic's Claude Mythos model — under the June 2, 2026 'Project Glasswing' collaboration with Anthropic — to cut safety-verification time for its software and social-infrastructure products from several weeks to a few hours. Applied to 100+ social-infrastructure cases, primarily energy-sector systems, generating proof-of-concept exploit code and detecting vulnerabilities with high precision across source trees comprising millions of lines. Hitachi frames the tool as augmenting, not replacing, human security experts for final risk assessment — the third Hitachi–Anthropic disclosure this year after the May 19 'Lumada 3.0' partnership and June 2 Project Glasswing announcement.

tags.l: NEDO silicon quantum lead w/ Intel + AIST
Human experts still required for final risk calls

entities.name: Toshiba
entities.desc: Industrial conglomerate taken private by the JIP consortium in 2023. Confirmed July 17, 2026 it is joining the NEDO-backed Noetra sovereign-AI project, adding another manufacturer with deep industrial and energy-sector data to the 44-company coalition. Participation signals the project's reach beyond listed AI names into Japan's legacy industrial base.

entities.name: Disco
entities.desc: Precision-processing equipment maker — dicing saws, grinders, polishers plus consumable blades and wheels ('Kiru, Kezuru, Migaku' 切る・削る・磨く) — with roughly 70–80% global share in its core niches and a structural role in AI back-end packaging (wafer thinning/grinding for HBM stacking). Q1 FY2026 (Apr–Jun) results released July 23, 2026: preliminary shipments hit a quarterly record ¥116.5bn (+25.3% YoY, above internal plan); Nikkei reported operating profit up ~40% YoY to ¥45bn+, beating the ¥42bn company plan, a record for the April–June quarter. First reporter of the July earnings gauntlet after the chip-complex correction; guides quarterly, so its Jul–Sep outlook is the read-through for AI-capex durability.

entities.name: GPIF
entities.zh: 年金積立金管理運用独立行政法人
entities.py: Nenkin Tsumitatekin Kanri Un'yō Dokuritsu Gyōsei Hōjin
entities.desc: Japan's Government Pension Investment Fund, managing ¥293.6T (March 2026) with a 25%-per-asset-class benchmark; domestic bonds stood at 26.9%. Focus of MOF's July 2026 domestic-buyer push: Katayama's July 10 remarks, the July 13 sourced walk-back of any benchmark overhaul, and her July 14–16 follow-ups keeping open a within-band domestic tilt. SocGen estimates a domestic rebalance could mean ~$76B of JGB buying.

entities.name: JPYC
entities.desc: Tokyo fintech issuing JPYC, the first yen-pegged stablecoin approved by the FSA under the revised Payment Services Act (資金決済法); launched October 27, 2025, registered as a Type II Funds Transfer Service Provider. On July 20, 2026 logistics group AZ-COM Maruwa said it will route outsourcing payments to ~2,300 carriers through JPYC with a ¥1B commitment — the first large-scale corporate B2B rollout of a yen stablecoin, moving it from crypto niche toward real settlement rails.

tags.l: Type II transfer caps limit ticket size

entities.name: AZ-COM Maruwa
entities.zh: AZ-COM丸和ホールディングス
entities.desc: Last-mile logistics group whose network delivers for Amazon Japan, relying on small trucking companies and owner-operator drivers. Announced (reported July 20, 2026 by Nikkei) it will invest ¥1B in JPYC and settle outsourcing fees to roughly 2,300 partner carriers on-chain in the yen stablecoin — Japan's first large-scale corporate stablecoin deployment, aimed at cutting transfer costs on high-frequency small payouts.

entities.name: FSA
entities.desc: Japan's Financial Services Agency. Its stablecoin regime under the revised Payment Services Act (資金決済法) — which made JPYC the first approved yen stablecoin in October 2025 — got its first large-scale corporate validation on July 20, 2026 when AZ-COM Maruwa committed to paying ~2,300 carriers in JPYC. The FSA framework's trust-backed, 1:1-redeemable design is becoming the template for yen settlement tokens, with megabank projects watching the rollout.

tags.l: Stablecoin regime gets first big corporate test

entities.name: METI
entities.desc: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, lead ministry for Japan's industrial and standardization policy. On July 21, 2026 the government said it will create a senior coordination post — a de facto standards czar — to push Japanese technology into international standards in AI and semiconductors, formalizing the 国際標準化 (kokusai hyōjunka) strategy that has so far run through the Hiroshima AI Process, the AI Safety Institute and ISO/IEC work. The post sits within the Takaichi government's ¥370tn 17-sector growth roadmap.

tags.l: Japan trails US/China de facto standards

entities.name: Advantest
entities.desc: World leader in semiconductor automated test equipment (ATE), with dominant share in testers for AI accelerators and HBM — making it one of the highest-beta AI names on the Tokyo exchange. Fell sharply in the July 24, 2026 AI-valuation rout alongside Tokyo Electron and Kioxia. Reports earnings the week of July 28 alongside SCREEN Holdings and Tokyo Electron, into a Nikkei that has lost more than 7% in July and slid into correction — making its order commentary a key read on whether AI-test demand is actually softening or just being repriced. **Q1 FY2026 results, first of the equipment gauntlet (#60, Jul 29 2026):** Reported record Q1 profit — EPS $1.51, net margin 33.2%, ROE 55.98% — on strong demand, favorable product mix and FX gains across CPU, GPU, custom-ASIC and networking testers. Management raised its view of the SoC tester market and said capacity expansion is being pulled forward. Shares still fell 1.22% to ¥25,200, as investors focused on a cautious margin outlook rather than the record top line — the first print in the Advantest (Jul 29) → Tokyo Electron (Jul 30) → Kioxia (Jul 31) equipment/memory earnings sequence that follows the July 28 CXMT-triggered sell-off. **FY2026 guidance raised 35% (#62, Jul 29-31 2026):** Follow-through from the Q1 print: management lifted full-year operating-profit guidance to ¥846.0bn on ¥1.714tn revenue — implying roughly 70% YoY growth, up from a prior forecast of about 26%, and above the ~42% consensus had modeled — after AI-inference tester demand outran what the company assumed as recently as April. Advantest also raised its view of the global semiconductor tester market to $13.0–14.5bn for the year, a record and about 19% above its April forecast. Shares jumped as much as 10.9% intraday on the update, part of a broader Nikkei rally (+4.0% Jul 31) that also lifted Tokyo Electron and Kioxia — a reversal from the cautious Jul 29 reaction and a reminder that the stock is trading on forward order-book signals as much as trailing results.

entities.name: Tokyo Electron
entities.desc: Japan's largest semiconductor-equipment maker (coaters/developers, etch, deposition) with near-100% share in EUV-line coater/developers — a core supplier to both the global logic ramp and Rapidus's 2nm effort. Sold off in the July 24, 2026 AI-valuation rout and reports earnings the week of July 28, one of the marquee prints of the semi-equipment earnings gauntlet that will test whether the AI-capex correction is sentiment or order-book reality. **July 28 sell-off, earnings Jul 30 (#59):** Fell 11.2% on July 28 as the CXMT STAR Market debut and renewed worry over China's domestic DUV lithography progress hit Japanese equipment names broadly; reports earnings July 30, immediately ahead of Kioxia (Jul 31) and inside the same week as the BOJ's policy meeting. **Kumamoto earthquake exposes equipment-side risk (#61, Jul 28-29, 2026):** Unlike JASM's sub-3%-of-capacity exposure, Tokyo Electron Kyushu — which holds a 91% global share of coater/developer equipment (the machines that apply and develop photoresist) — suspended both its Kumamoto facilities on Jul 29 for precautionary safety inspections after the M7.1 quake, with no major damage confirmed as of the halt. Because TEL Kyushu's coater/developer share is close to a monopoly position in the global lithography line, any extended stoppage — even without physical damage — is a more consequential supply-chain signal than the TSMC fab-safety headline; this is the name to watch for updates on when Kyushu output resumes. **Q1 FY2027 record results, 5-for-1 split (#64, Jul 30 2026):** Reported record quarterly revenue of ¥732.3bn (+2.9% QoQ, +33.3% YoY) and record gross profit of ¥342.7bn, driven by AI-data-center-linked WFE demand — non-memory (logic) 57% of sales, DRAM 32% (HBM-linked). Sharply raised first-half (Apr-Sep) guidance to revenue of ¥1.62tn and operating profit of ¥458bn (28.3% margin), both would-be half-year records; new equipment sales guided to ¥1.24tn, +45% YoY. Management reiterated FY2027 mid-term targets (revenue >¥3tn, operating margin ≥35%, ROE ≥30%) and set a new goal of gross margin >50% within two years (from ~46.8% in Q1). Announced a 5-for-1 stock split (record date Sept 30, 2026) to broaden its individual-investor base, alongside a record ¥384/share interim dividend and a ¥150bn buyback. Also disclosed an expanded NVIDIA collaboration this month targeting agentic-AI and robotics-linked equipment services. Shares rose on the print, part of a broader Nikkei semiconductor rally; management flagged no material impact so far from Middle East or US-China tensions.

entities.name: SoftBank Corp
entities.desc: Telecom operator repositioning as Japan's enterprise AI-security and AI-agent channel (distinct from parent SoftBank Group, TSE: 9984). On July 21, 2026 it disclosed first metrics for Patching as a Service, the OpenAI-powered vulnerability-assessment-to-patch offering run with JV SB OAI Japan: 137 assessment requests in the initial rollout, ~280 vulnerabilities found per 10 million lines of source code, expansion to 3,000 eligible companies with a ~1,000-person delivery team. Internally, OpenAI cyber tooling found 10,500 vulnerabilities across 700 SoftBank systems. Also announced exclusive Japan distribution of Sierra's conversational AI agent platform (pilot: 97% inquiry resolution, 93% CSAT).

entities.name: SB OAI Japan
entities.desc: SoftBank–OpenAI joint venture commercializing OpenAI technology for Japanese enterprises. Operates Patching as a Service (launched June 16, 2026) — AI vulnerability assessment through patch deployment — now expanding to 3,000 eligible companies with a ~1,000-person team per SoftBank's July 21, 2026 disclosure. Positioned by CEO Miyakawa as a 'vaccine for enterprise systems' against AI-driven cyberattacks; also the vehicle for the 'modernization for the AI era' source-code replacement push.

entities.name: Cabinet Office (CEFP)
entities.zh: 内閣府・経済財政諮問会議
entities.desc: Drafting body for the annual Basic Policy on Economic and Fiscal Management and Reform (骨太の方針). The Takaichi cabinet approved its first edition July 21, 2026: 'responsible and proactive fiscal policy,' ~¥370tn in public-private investment into strategic sectors including AI and semiconductors through FY2040, targets of >1% real and >3% nominal growth, and — notably — removal of the phrase 'fiscal consolidation' in favor of a stable-reduction anchor on the debt-to-GDP ratio. Bond market response was wary, with the long-term rate near 30-year highs and BOJ-independence questions unresolved ahead of the July 30 MPM. **Approval rating slide (#58, Jul 26-27 2026):** A Yomiuri poll fielded Jul 24-26 showed cabinet approval falling to 57% from 69% in June — the first sub-60% reading since Takaichi took office — with disapproval of cost-of-living policy rising to 71% from 56%. The government has delayed its pledged cut to the 8% food consumption-tax rate amid intra-LDP resistance and bond-market sensitivity, leaving the honebuto's ¥370tn growth pledge harder to square with near-term household relief.

entities.name: Sakana AI
entities.desc: Tokyo-based foundation-model startup founded by ex-Google Brain researchers David Ha and Llion Jones, known for evolutionary model-merging techniques and, most recently, the Fugu-Cyber security model. Increasingly used by Tokyo as a shop-window for Japanese AI abroad: Sakana attended the first Japan–France high-level AI talks in Paris in June 2026 alongside SoftBank, part of a Japanese push to build AI dialogue frameworks with Europe and Global South partners rather than depend solely on US and Chinese model providers. **Fugu adds Nemotron specialists (#62, Jul 2026):** Sakana confirmed plans to route select subtasks — coding, tool-calling, instruction-following — from its Fugu multi-agent orchestrator to NVIDIA's open-weight Nemotron models, alongside its own and other frontier models accessed through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The move, grounded in Sakana's ICLR 2026 papers on learned orchestration (TRINITY, the Conductor), is pitched as proof that a coordinated pool of open models can match proprietary single-model performance without vendor lock-in — a pitch aimed as much at enterprise buyers wary of over-indexing on one lab as at NVIDIA's push to keep its silicon relevant across the open-model stack. **Sakana Namazu API launch (#65, Aug 3, 2026):** Sakana AI opened Sakana Namazu, its Japanese-specialized LLM, as a commercial API for developers and enterprises — built on Moonshot AI's open-weight Kimi K2.6 base, then fine-tuned on proprietary internal data for Japanese-language nuance, business-context understanding, and agentic tool use. Sakana reports the tuned model beats its Kimi K2.6 base on JFBench (Japanese instruction-following) and posts a jump on FairPoliticsQA neutrality testing (34.10% to 56.30%), while holding onto Kimi K2.6's underlying reasoning/coding benchmark scores (AIME26, MMLU-Pro, LiveCodeBench v6). Positioned against the small set of high-tier Japanese-language LLM APIs, with pricing pitched below frontier-model rates. A second, distinct commercialization track from Fugu's open-model orchestration play (#62) — Namazu is a direct-to-enterprise API product, not a routing layer.

entities.name: NEC
entities.desc: IT services, biometrics and communications-infrastructure group; developer of the lightweight cotomi LLM (13B parameters, top-tier Japanese proficiency) and a core Noetra member alongside SoftBank, Sony and Honda. Shares are down ~20% from end-2025 versus a ~30% Nikkei gain on the 'AI eats IT services' thesis — that generative AI code-generation undercuts labor-based system-integration economics. CEO Takayuki Morita (森田隆之) pushed back in a Nikkei interview published July 23, 2026, arguing AI raises delivery productivity and that NEC's proprietary franchises (biometrics, government systems, defense, comms) are not commoditized by code-gen. Cleanest Tokyo expression of the global AI-vs-SIer de-rating trade.

entities.name: Ministry of Finance (Japan)
entities.desc: Owns Japan's foreign-exchange policy and authorises intervention, which the BOJ executes as its agent. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama (片山さつき) escalated verbal intervention on July 24, 2026 as USD/JPY approached 164, saying authorities would 'take resolute actions decisively' if needed, and noting Japanese and US authorities were 'on the same page' after the US Treasury called excess yen volatility undesirable. The Treasury report put the yen's decline at 51% against the dollar between end-2011 and end-April 2026 in both nominal and real effective terms, describing 'substantial yen undervaluation.' **Yen/JGB backdrop into the July 30-31 BOJ meeting (#60):** USD/JPY traded near ¥163.7 on July 29, its worst week since May and closing in on the psychologically watched ¥165 level, with verbal warnings so far doing little to deter yen bears. The 40-year JGB yield climbed 10bp to 4.01% on July 24, nearing its May record of 4.355%, as bond markets stayed skeptical that the BOJ is tightening fast enough to offset a government that is simultaneously raising spending (the ¥370tn honebuto roadmap) and stalling its consumption-tax relief pledge. The MOF's intervention rhetoric and the BOJ's rate path are now being priced as substitutes rather than complements. **Suspected ambush intervention, Jul 30 2026 (#62):** The dollar posted its steepest single-session drop against the yen since 2022 during July 30 US trading — a synchronized move across major yen pairs that FX desks at BBVA, TJM and SBI FX Trade attributed to unconfirmed MOF action, arriving just ahead of the July 30-31 BOJ meeting and consistent with the ministry's pattern of unannounced 'ambush' operations rather than pre-signaled ones. MOF has not confirmed the operation, in keeping with standard practice; official confirmation, if any, will only appear in the ministry's monthly intervention disclosure, typically released weeks later. The episode shows that verbal warnings and the BOJ's 1% rate hold were not, on their own, enough to stop the yen's slide toward the 163-165 zone — forcing MOF back into the market days after its last confirmed round. **June trade balance swings to deficit (#63, released Jul 30 2026):** MOF/Customs data showed a ¥409.9bn trade deficit for June, reversing a ¥122.3bn surplus a year earlier and far worse than the ~¥120bn deficit consensus expected. Exports rose 19.3% YoY to ¥10.93tn (a three-year high, tenth straight month of growth) on weak-yen-inflated receipts and AI-chip demand — semiconductor exports +53.8% YoY, semiconductor-manufacturing-equipment exports +18.7%. But imports rose faster, +25.4% YoY to ¥11.34tn: mineral fuels +41.9% (petroleum +59.3%, coal +46.8%, an Iran-conflict energy-price effect) and semiconductor imports +49.2% — Japan is simultaneously a net AI-chip exporter and a large AI-chip importer, so the 'AI boom' shows up on both sides of the trade ledger. Net effect: a weak yen (~¥163/USD) is inflating nominal export values without necessarily improving Japan's real trade position, and the energy-import bill is the main swing factor pulling the balance negative — a data point MOF and the BOJ will weigh alongside intervention and rate-path decisions. **Joint US-Japan yen intervention, first since 2011 (#64, Aug 2 2026):** Finance Minister Katayama announced Tokyo and Washington undertook joint action to arrest the yen's slide toward 40-year lows (near ¥163-165/USD) — the first coordinated Japan-US currency intervention since 2011. BOJ data suggest Japan sold as much as $58.97bn for yen in the operation, which Katayama said began in New York trading hours and 'is still ongoing.' The intervention followed the BOJ's July 31 hold at 1.00% and came alongside signals from Ueda's press conference that a rate hike could follow soon — pairing currency defense with rate-path signaling for the first time this cycle. Distinct from MOF's unconfirmed 'ambush' interventions in April-May and July: this one was explicitly announced and coordinated with the US Treasury, a materially higher-commitment signal than prior unilateral, unannounced operations.

entities.name: Nautilus Technologies
entities.zh: ノーティラス・テクノロジーズ
entities.desc: Tokyo-based distributed-computing and networking startup, previously known for KYOJO CUP low-latency video/telemetry systems for motorsport. Lead technical partner (with Internet Initiative Japan, IIJ) in a NEDO-backed proof-of-concept launched July 27, 2026 for a next-generation distributed AI processing infrastructure realizing Japan's 'watt-bit' (ワット・ビット) vision — combining TEPCO Power Grid and Chubu Electric Power Grid optical fiber with Fujitsu/1FINITY communications gear into an all-photonics network (APN) linking GPU servers across two utility supply areas. The trial used the KYOJO CUP season finale at Fuji Speedway as a live 4K-video/telemetry test load, assessing whether low-latency distributed AI processing can double as a grid demand-response resource.

entities.name: Renesas Electronics
entities.zh: ルネサスエレクトロニクス
entities.desc: Japan's largest microcontroller (MCU) maker, with heavy exposure to automotive and industrial chips as well as growing AI-accelerator-adjacent product lines. Fell 10.6% on July 28, 2026 in the broad Asian semiconductor sell-off triggered by China's CXMT STAR Market debut (a $487B-market-cap DRAM listing that revived oversupply and China-competitiveness concerns) and renewed worry over Nvidia's circular AI-financing arrangements; the drop contributed to the Nikkei 225's 4.16% fall to 62,230, its lowest close in more than two months. **Kumamoto earthquake plant checks (#61, Jul 28-29, 2026):** Following the Jul 28 M7.1 quake, Renesas began assessing conditions at its Kawashiri plant (Kumamoto City) and Nishiki plant (Nishiki), both of which produce semiconductor-related products; no damage or production-halt confirmation was available on the day of the checks. Adds a second, quake-driven overhang on top of the Jul 28 CXMT-triggered sell-off — worth tracking whether Renesas confirms any output impact in the days after. **Sues Navitas over GaN trade secrets (#65, reported Jul 22, filed Jul 29 2026):** Renesas filed suit against US-based Navitas Semiconductor in the Northern District of California, alleging Navitas CEO Christopher Allexandre and executive Felicia Cheng — both former Renesas employees — took confidential PowerPoint presentations containing Renesas's GaN (gallium nitride) power-chip roadmap for AI data centers before joining Navitas, and that Navitas's subsequent '2.0' strategy mirrors those stolen plans' target customers and technologies. Renesas seeks damages and an injunction against further use. The dispute sits directly on top of the AI-data-center power opportunity both companies are chasing: Renesas's own data-center segment is a structural growth driver (Q1 FY2026 revenue +23.2% YoY to ¥380.3bn, guided to keep growing on AI/data-center and automotive demand), while Navitas has repositioned almost entirely around GaN/SiC for 800V AI data-center power architectures (Q2 2026 revenue +22% QoQ, guiding AI-related revenue above a third of sales by year-end). For investors, the case is as much a signal of how contested next-gen data-center power silicon has become as it is a legal filing — Navitas has said it will contest the allegations.

tags.l: Sues Navitas over GaN trade secrets

entities.name: KDDI Corporation
entities.desc: Japan's second-largest telecom carrier (au, UQ mobile, povo) and a 15-year open-innovation investor via its KDDI Open Innovation Fund. **AI Startup Support Program with Google AI Futures Fund (#61, Jul 28, 2026):** KDDI and Google AI Futures Fund launched a joint investment program for Japanese AI startups, combining direct equity funding from both parties with early access to Google DeepMind models (Gemini, Nano Banana, Lyria), trial access to 'Gemini on GDC' — an on-premises sovereign Gemini instance provisioned in Japan via KDDI's Osaka-Sakai Data Center — and KDDI GPU Cloud infrastructure, plus hands-on technical support from Google and KDDI engineers. Builds on KDDI's ¥30B startup-ecosystem commitment announced April 2025 and its push since 2025 to deepen ties with US venture capital for cross-border support. Applications opened Jul 28, 2026.

entities.name: SB Intuitions
entities.desc: SoftBank Corp subsidiary building Japanese-language foundation models. Trains its Sarashina (さらしな) LLM series on NVIDIA Nemotron tooling — primarily the NeMo RL post-training library and Megatron-LM for large-scale distributed training. **Large Telecom Model / LTM (#63, reported Jul 20 2026):** Combined Sarashina with the Nemotron stack to build a foundation model specialized for telecom-network operations automation — SoftBank's attempt to turn its own carrier infrastructure into a proprietary AI training ground. Positions SB Intuitions as the model-development arm feeding SoftBank Group's broader sovereign-AI ambitions (Noetra, physical AI), while remaining structurally reliant on NVIDIA's open-source training stack rather than building entirely from scratch.

entities.name: Institute of Science Tokyo
entities.desc: National research university (merger of Tokyo Institute of Technology and Tokyo Medical and Dental University) developing Swallow, an open Japanese-language foundation model. **Nemotron-trained (#63, reported Jul 20 2026):** Uses NVIDIA Nemotron datasets in both pre-training and post-training of the Swallow series, which is positioned as a leading open model for Japanese-language processing. Also a named participant, alongside AIST, Cambridge and Oxford, in Japan's government-backed physical-AI research framework spanning 13 international institutions.

entities.name: Stockmark
entities.desc: Tokyo AI startup selected for METI's GENIAC foundation-model development support program. **Stockmark-Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-JapanDocReader (#63, Jul 15-20 2026):** Released a visual-language model built on NVIDIA's open Nemotron 3 Nano Omni model, specialized for reading and structuring Japanese business documents — a niche (structured-document extraction) underserved by general-purpose frontier models. Also developing enterprise knowledge-retrieval applications using NVIDIA NeMo Retriever, serving manufacturing, energy and chemical-sector clients. Small-scale example of the same pattern as larger domestic players: GENIAC-backed 'sovereign' model development still runs on NVIDIA's open Nemotron ecosystem.
